question: On the first Republic Day, 26 January 1950, the Constitution of India replaced which British Act?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act (1935)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act (1935) was the last pre-independence constitution of India.
 
• It was the longest act (with 321 sections and 10 schedules) enacted by the British Parliament for India.
 
• This act provided the framework for the establishment of an all-India federation and provincial autonomy.
 
• Many features of the Government of India Act (1935) were later incorporated into the Constitution of India, which came into effect on 26 January 1950.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act (1919)**

 
 
• Also known as the Montague-Chelmsford Reforms, it introduced a dual form of government (diarchy) for the major provinces.
 
• Under this act, provincial subjects were divided into two categories: transferred and reserved.
 
• The act aimed to increase Indian participation in the administration and introduced the concept of a bicameral legislature at the Centre.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act (1858)**
 
 
• It marked the end of the East India Company's rule and transferred control of India to the British Crown.
 
• The office of the Secretary of State for India was established and vested with complete authority and control over the Indian administration.
 
• This act also created the office of the Viceroy of India, who was the Crown's representative.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act (1930)**
 
 
• There is no specific Government of India Act of 1930. It is likely a typographical error in the options provided.
